snip.t: Susceptibility to T1DM is genetically controlled by alleles of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II genes expressing human leukocyte antigens (HLAs).

It recognizes antigens presented on major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II molecules and secretes cytokines (interferon-gamma, interleukin-2) to activate macrophages, cytotoxic CD8+ T-cells, and natural killer (NK) cells.

These include the class II, major histocompatibility complex, transactivator (CIITA), C-type lectin domain family 16, member A (CLEC16A ), and protein tyrosine phosphatase, nonreceptor type 22 (PTPN22).

snip.t: Downregulating MHC I: Many viruses reduce the expression of Major Histocompatibility Complex class I molecules on the surface of infected cells, preventing cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) from recognizing and killing the infected cells.

snip.t: Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs) and Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules work together in a sophisticated system to prevent the spread of infections through effective immune surveillance and response coordination.

qs.q: Which of the following host cell types expresses major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II molecules to present exogenous antigens specifically to CD4+ T helper cells?
o: Endothelial cells lining the vascular system
All nucleated human cells expressing the marker
Red blood cells circulating throughout the body
qs.e: MHC class II molecules are expressed exclusively on antigen-presenting cells (APCs) to present exogenous antigens to CD4+ T cells. MHC class I molecules are expressed on all nucleated cells to present endogenous antigens.

qs.q: The Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) genes are highly polymorphic. What does 'polymorphic' mean in this context?
o: They can switch their gene segments during development.
They have multiple alleles within the population.
They are highly conserved among individuals.
They encode enzymes involved in antigen processing.
qs.e: Polymorphism refers to the existence of multiple different alleles (variants) for a gene within a population. The high polymorphism of MHC genes ensures that a wide variety of peptides can be presented, contributing to population-level immunity.
